In each participating school, teams of core content teachers share a common cohort of approximately 85 to 100 ninth grade students. This structure allows teachers to collaborate weekly, coordinate instruction, and respond collectively to student needs rather than working in isolation.

World History I and Algebra I serve as anchor courses across all three sites with additional subjects such as English 9, Health and PE 9, Environmental Studies, and Biology woven in to create opportunities for cross-curricular alignment and more coherent learning experiences that serve to amplify the Henrico learner profile by bringing it to life for students. Together, these teams function as a professional learning community centered on shared students, shared goals, and shared responsibility. Their partnership has not only strengthened teacher satisfaction

and efficacy, but has also created a connected, supportive learner-centered community where students feel known, supported, and set up for success. This targeted approach for developing the durable skills of the HLP also amplifies the best practices of the instructional model.
